'''Charles Emery Roberts Jr.''' (October 9, 1942 – March 26, 2023) was an American [[mathematician]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=Theodore Dreiser Distinguished Research/Creativity Awards presented {{!}} Newsroom {{!}} Indiana State University |url=https://news.indianastate.edu/2010/04/29/theodore-dreiser-distinguished-researchcreativity-awards-presented |website=news.indianastate.edu |publisher=Indiana State University |access-date=14 January 2026 |language=en |date=29 April 2010}}</ref> He was a professor of mathematics at [[Indiana State University]] from 1971 to 2017. He developed the [[Jacchia Reference Atmosphere|Jacchia-Roberts Atmospheric Model]] used widely for [[orbit determination]] and spacecraft [[atmospheric entry]] simulations in [[aerospace]].

==Early life and education==
Roberts was born in 1942 in [[Washington, D.C.]] to Evelyn and Charles Roberts Sr.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Obituary information for Charles E. Roberts, Jr. |url=https://www.friedrichjones.com/obituaries/Charles-E-Roberts-Jr?obId=27604419 |website=www.friedrichjones.com |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He attended [[North Posey High School]] and graduated as valedictorian in 1960.<ref name=":1" /> He studied mathematics at [[Indiana State University]], where he graduated [[summa cum laude]] in 1964 before attending the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], where he earned a master's in 1965.<ref name=":0" /> He studied under [[Geneva G. Belford]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Geneva Belford, 1932-2014 |url=https://siebelschool.illinois.edu/news/geneva-belford-1932-2014 |website=siebelschool.illinois.edu |publisher=Grainger Engineering Office of Marketing and Communications |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and produced a thesis on the [[integral curve]]s of [[differential equations]], earning a doctorate in 1968.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Doctoral Graduates {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} Illinois |url=https://math.illinois.edu/academics/graduate-program/doctoral-graduates |website=math.illinois.edu |access-date=14 January 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==

After graduating from the University of Illinois, Roberts began working with [[Pan-American Airlines]] in [[Cape Canaveral Space Force Station|Cape Canaveral, Florida]] from 1968 to 1970. He wrote satellite tracking programs in conjunction with [[NASA]] during the Apollo missions, including [[Apollo 11]].<ref name=":2" />

In 1971, he returned to Indiana State and became a professor of mathematics. Roberts wrote multiple textbooks on [[mathematical proof]]s and [[differential equation]]s.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Böhme |first1=S. |last2=Fricke |first2=W. |last3=Güntzel-Lingner |first3=U. |last4=Henn |first4=F. |last5=Krahn |first5=D. |last6=Scheffer |first6=U. |last7=Zech |first7=G. |title=Literature 1971, Part 2 |date=11 November 2013 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-662-12278-5 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Literature_1971_Part_2/x6XyCAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=c.e.+roberts+jacchia&pg=PA211&printsec=frontcover |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In 1971, he published a modified version of the [[reference atmosphere]] developed by [[Luigi Giuseppe Jacchia]] in 1970.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Canuto |first1=Enrico |last2=Novara |first2=Carlo |last3=Carlucci |first3=Donato |last4=Perez-Montenegro |first4=Carlos |last5=Massotti |first5=Luca |title=Spacecraft Dynamics and Control: The Embedded Model Control Approach |date=8 March 2018 |publisher=Butterworth-Heinemann |isbn=978-0-08-101795-1 |page=163 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Spacecraft_Dynamics_and_Control/cycsDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=c.e.+roberts+jacchia&pg=PA184&printsec=frontcover |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In it, he used an [[asymptotic function]] to derive an integrable form of the [[differential equation]]s used to model [[Barometric formula|barometric]] and [[molecular diffusion]] in the [[upper atmosphere]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cappellari |first1=J. O. |last2=Vélez |first2=C. E. |last3=Fuchs |first3=Arthur J. |title=Mathematical Theory of the Goddard Trajectory Determination System |date=1976 |publisher=Goddard Space Flight Center |page=33 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Mathematical_Theory_of_the_Goddard_Traje/-r6WsbfnrQIC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=c.e.+roberts+jacchia&pg=SA4-PA33&printsec=frontcover |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> The Jacchia-Roberts Density Model is widely used in aerospace applications to model satellite orbital decay, compute [[orbit determination]], and re-entry trajectories.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Roberts |first1=Charles E. |title=An analytic model for upper atmosphere densities based upon Jacchia's 1970 models |journal=Celestial mechanics |date=1 December 1971 |volume=4 |issue=3 |pages=368–377 |doi=10.1007/BF01231398 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01231398 |access-date=14 January 2026 |language=en |issn=1572-9478|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Gurfil |first1=Pini |title=Modern Astrodynamics |date=19 October 2006 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-08-046491-6 |pages=8–11 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Modern_Astrodynamics/vwir24X66sQC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=c.e.+roberts+jacchia&pg=PA8&printsec=frontcover |access-date=20 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Lara |first1=Martin |title=Hamiltonian Perturbation Solutions for Spacecraft Orbit Prediction |date=2021 |publisher=de Gruyter |page=243 |edition=1 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Hamiltonian_Perturbation_Solutions_for_S/z9IuEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=c.e.+roberts+jacchia&pg=PA363&printsec=frontcover |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref>

He also published papers on celestial mechanics and developed methods for using power series to generate trajectories for orbital and suborbital vehicles.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Roberts |first1=Charles E. |title=Comments on the application of power series solutions to problems in celestial mechanics |journal=Celestial mechanics |date=1 December 1975 |volume=12 |issue=4 |pages=397–407 |doi=10.1007/BF01595387 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01595387 |access-date=14 January 2026 |language=en |issn=1572-9478|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His mathematics research also dealt with Hammerstein operators<ref>{{cite journal |last1=de Korvin |first1=Andre |last2=Roberts |first2=Charles E. |title=Double adjoints of Hammerstein functionals defined on continuous functions |journal=Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata |date=1 December 1980 |volume=126 |issue=1 |pages=93–102 |doi=10.1007/BF01762502 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01762502 |access-date=14 January 2026 |language=en |issn=1618-1891}}</ref> and combinatorial theory.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Roberts |first1=Charles E |title=Sets of mutually orthogonal Latin squares with “like subsquares” |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A |date=1 September 1992 |volume=61 |issue=1 |pages=50–63 |doi=10.1016/0097-3165(92)90052-V |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/009731659290052V |access-date=14 January 2026 |issn=0097-3165|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Roberts received the [[Theodore Dreiser]] Distinguished Research Award in 2010. He retired in 2017.<ref name=":2" />

Roberts died in 2023 in [[Naperville, Illinois]], aged 80.<ref name=":1" />

== Personal life ==

He married Imogene Roberts on August 25, 1963. They lived in [[Terre Haute, Indiana]] and were married for 59 years until her death two weeks before his own. According to his wishes, his body was donated to the Anatomical Gift Association of [[Chicago]].<ref name=":1" />

== Books ==
* ''Ordinary Differential Equations: A Computation Approach'' ([[Prentice Hall]], 1979) {{ISBN|9780136397571}}
* ''Elementary Differential Equations: Applications, Models, and Computing'' ([[Chapman & Hall]], 2010) {{ISBN|9781041151463}}
* ''Introduction to Mathematical Proofs'' ([[Chapman & Hall]], 2015) {{ISBN|9781032920238}}
